title: "I Built a Free Password Generator — No Signup, No Subscription"

published: true

tags: [showdev, security, webdev, javascript]

As a developer and a user of numerous online services, I've come to realize the importance of having strong, unique passwords for each account. However, generating and remembering these passwords can be a daunting task. This is why I built a free password generator that can be used by anyone, without the need for signups or subscriptions. You can try it out right now at https://password-generator.solomontools.workers.dev.

Introduction to the Problem

We've all been there - trying to come up with a password that meets the requirements of being at least 12 characters long, containing uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. It's not only frustrating but also insecure to use the same password across multiple sites or to use weak passwords that can be easily guessed. The solution to this problem is to use a password generator that can create cryptographically strong passwords.

How it Works

Under the hood, my password generator utilizes Cloudflare Workers, which provide a serverless platform for building applications. This allows the generator to run at the edge, reducing latency and improving performance. The password generation algorithm itself relies on AI inference to ensure that the passwords are not only strong but also unique.

The basic architecture of the password generator can be represented as follows:

// Generate a password of a specified length
async function generatePassword(length) {
const characters = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789!@#$%^&*()_+~`|}{[]:;?><,./-=';
let password = '';
for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) {
password += characters.charAt(Math.floor(Math.random() * characters.length));
}
return password;
}

This is a simplified example, and the actual implementation includes additional checks and balances to ensure the generated passwords meet the required security standards.

Building the Tool

When building the password generator, I focused on creating a user-friendly interface that would allow users to customize the length of their passwords. The tool also includes a feature to automatically copy the generated password to the clipboard, making it easier to use the password without having to manually type it out.

One of the challenges I faced while building the tool was ensuring that the password generation algorithm was secure and unbiased. To address this, I implemented a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) to generate the passwords. This ensures that the passwords are truly random and unpredictable.

Shipping the Tool

Shipping the password generator was a straightforward process, thanks to Cloudflare Workers. I was able to deploy the application to the edge, where it can be accessed by users from all over the world. The serverless architecture of Cloudflare Workers also means that I don't have to worry about scaling the application, as it can handle a large number of requests without any issues.

What I Learned

Throughout the process of building and shipping the password generator, I learned a lot about the importance of security and usability. I realized that even small tools like a password generator can make a big difference in helping users protect their online accounts. I also learned about the capabilities of Cloudflare Workers and how they can be used to build scalable and secure applications.

Conclusion

In conclusion, my password generator is a free tool that can be used by anyone to generate cryptographically strong passwords. It's customizable, secure, and easy to use. If you're tired of using weak passwords or struggling to come up with unique passwords for each of your online accounts, give it a try at https://password-generator.solomontools.workers.dev.
